_comment: The CatHarness declaration for THIS instance — what directories it scans and what kind of graph each holds. See skills/folio-core/directory-conventions.md. This repo is PRE-SPLIT (issue #223), so it declares what is true today, not the target layout: `tools/` and `folio/` do not exist here yet and are deliberately not declared. A directory that is declared but absent is worse than one that is missing, because every consumer then scans nothing and reports a clean run over it. NOTE: `schemas/` declares TWO graphs — the first real use of the array. A directory is a place to look and may hold more than one part of the graph; it does not say how to tell them apart, because the files declare what they are (see bean xxxb: schemas/*.ts does not yet do this well). `beans/` is declared ONCE, as a single `beans` graph. Its internal split — `defs` for work items, `workflows` for running BPMN state — is declared by `beans/beans.json`, not here. #263 declared the two as separate directories, one nested inside the other, which left a consumer unable to tell which owned what beneath it; the nodes now carry that.

images.description: An at-sign whose inner a is a cat: the a's bowl is the head, its counter is the face, the ears grow out of the top of the bowl and cross the ring, and the whiskers are cut in white across the sage. The ring keeps its gap and its tail, so it still reads as an @.

images.title: Thinking about it
images.description: The landing backdrop, wide crop. A grumpy cat in a sage hoodie stands in the rain under a thought-cloud carrying the c@t mark; the instance's description is drawn inside the cloud. The text region is the cloud's lower interior, below the mark and clear of the ear that rises into the lower left — found by rendering candidate boxes over the image and looking at them, which is the only way to find it.

directories.description: Tool definitions — one concrete way to exercise a skill, each naming the skills it satisfies. Authored as .ts calling defineTool so a malformed node fails at tsc; the JSON-LD and JSON Schema renderings are generated.

The content-object model and the per-skill JSON Schemas. Declares BOTH graphs: the schema definitions themselves, and `kg` because a schema IS a knowledge-graph node — the .ts files are part of the KG, not a separate island beside it.

The knowledge graph. Skill packages, and the four other node kinds that point at them: `roles/roles.json` (a role IS a BPMN swimlane, and carries the skills its lane's activities need), `workflows/*.bpmn` + `workflows/decisions/*.dmn` (the processes those roles act in, reached through the skill that describes them), `requirements/*.json` (conformance obligations whose `satisfiedBy` names the skill or capability discharging them), `permissions/permissions.json` (what an actor may DO in any lane, as opposed to what its lane's role knows), and the `kg-qa/` audit sidecars beside each. Note the id is `kg` while the path is `skills/` — ids are stable across a relocation, paths are not.
The work plan. `beans/beans.json` declares its nodes — `defs` (work items) and `workflows` (running BPMN instance state).
